jobs.description:
Our Mission

American Fork City's mission is to provide excellence in service to residents, visitors, and business community to foster a high quality of life.

What You’ll Deliver

American Fork City is hiring an entry-level GIS Technician to support accurate, up-to-date GIS information that helps City teams plan, review, and communicate infrastructure data. This role exists to keep spatial records reliable, searchable, and ready for engineering and public-facing needs.

Key Responsibilities Include

Create and maintain digitized maps and spatial layers using ArcGIS and ArcGIS Online
Produce map outputs and graphics for projects; support drafting needs with AutoCAD Map 3D
Organize and update data base content; perform quality checks and version control
Research and interpret blueprints, plans, and drawings; document findings clearly
Use Python and Arcade for workflow support and attribute logic when needed

Required Qualifications/skills

High school diploma plus two years technical training in computer science, or an associate degree in computer science (GIS specialization) and one year of experience
Working knowledge of Windows, Excel, Office, ArcGIS, ArcGIS Online, Python, and Arcade
Understanding of GIS concepts, procedures, and design methods

Apply to help strengthen the City’s GIS mapping and data accuracy.

How Your Day Flows

You’ll start onsite in American Fork by reviewing incoming requests and prioritizing GIS updates. Most of the day is spent building or refining map layers in ArcGIS, checking attributes, and validating geometry so the information is dependable. You’ll shift between screens and source materials—plans, drawings, and field notes—then translate them into clean, standardized records. When a map needs a polished finish, you’ll format graphics for clear distribution and, as needed, move into AutoCAD Map 3D to align drafting outputs. You’ll also spend focused time tightening datasets, keeping the data base organized, and using ArcGIS Online to publish or refresh content for internal use.

Benefits That Support You

Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage; 401(k); Life Insurance; Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA); Competitive Salary; Paid Time Off; Employee Discounts; URS retirement benefits; and an American Fork Fitness Center pass.

Overview

The Waste Management and Prevention Division of the Department of Environmental Conservation (DEC) is seeking a highly motivated, organized, and detailed-oriented individual to fill an Environmental Analyst IV position in the Hazardous Materials Program. This position will work alongside an experienced technical team and conduct independent environmental compliance inspections for hazardous waste management and underground fuel storage tanks, as well as review and issue construction permits. The Program currently regulates over 3,000 facilities that generate hazardous waste and approximately 750 underground storage tank facilities, such as gas stations; these facilities are located throughout the State. This position is critically important to Vermont's environment and public health by preventing releases of hazardous materials and leaks from underground storage tanks to the environment. This position requires state-wide travel to a variety of Vermont businesses and offers the ability to create your own field schedule.

An Ideal Applicant Will Have

Knowledge of or experience working with underground storage tank (UST) systems and operations and or experience with hazardous waste generation and management
Experience in conducting environmental field work, both independently and/or as part of a team
Basic knowledge of state and federal storage tanks rules and hazardous waste regulations
Experience with and interest in environmental compliance and enforcement activities
Strong technical writing skills and effective verbal communication skills with diverse audiences
Experience with drafting regulatory permits
An interest in protecting Vermont's environment and public health

The position will involve both field compliance work and office work. This position is based in Montpelier.

Submitting a cover letter that outlines the applicant's qualification for and interest in the position is strongly encouraged.

Who May Apply

This position, Environmental Analyst IV - Hazardous Materials Program (Job Requisition #55524)
, is open to all State employees and external applicants.

If you would like more information about this position, please contact Michael.Nucci@vermont.gov.

Resumes will not be accepted via e-mail. You must apply online to be considered.

Please note that multiple positions in the same work location may be filled from this job posting.

Field work may involve exposure to chemicals, gases, hazardous liquid and solid waste, construction sites during all weather conditions and may involve traversing rough terrain and bodies of water. Some work outside of regular working hours, including attendance at public meetings, may be required. Strong differences of opinion may be encountered on a regular basis.

Minimum Qualifications

Master's degree or higher in a biological-life or physical science, engineering, a social science, data science, or an environmental or natural resources field.

OR

OR

American Fork City's mission is to provide excellence in service to residents, visitors, and business community to foster a high quality of life.

American Fork City is hiring an entry-level GIS Technician to support accurate, up-to-date GIS information that helps City teams plan, review, and communicate infrastructure data. This role exists to keep spatial records reliable, searchable, and ready for engineering and public-facing needs.

Key Responsibilities Include

Create and maintain digitized maps and spatial layers using ArcGIS and ArcGIS Online
Produce map outputs and graphics for projects; support drafting needs with AutoCAD Map 3D
Organize and update data base content; perform quality checks and version control
Research and interpret blueprints, plans, and drawings; document findings clearly

Job Description

Performs responsible staff work performing varied assignments in relieving a high-level administrator of administrative detail. Essential Functions/ Job Competencies/ Physical Requirements

ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Reviews and processes contractors/sub-recipients request for reimbursements.
Assists with preparing files for review boards approval and the bidding process.
Prepares loan documents and executes closings.
Manages delinquent accounts.
Inputs and monitors IDIS activities.
Assists with sub-recipients remote and/or on-site monitoring.

Develops and assists in the development of new methods and procedures for program, project, or functional operations; evaluates methods and recommends modifications as necessary.
Develops, prepares, maintains, processes, and distributes various reports, records, legal documents, analysis, and other documents pertinent to the programs or projects smooth operation; ensures same is in compliance with local, state, and federal laws, as well as, contact and program requirements.

Assists in maintaining good communication between staff, visitors, and other business contacts.
Responsible for reviewing the eligibility and completion of project files for various CD programs.
Assists in reviewing applications, contracts, leases, legal instruments, tax statements, and other related documents.
Submits eligible applications for funding; follows-up on pending applications and notifies applicants of status; secures additional documentation from applicant as needed.
Assists in marketing efforts for the department's program.
Prepares requisitions for the purpose of materials, supplies, and services as needed.
